methods.source: func testShortcutDispatch() { var s = 0; let r = row(save: {s += 1}); XCTAssertEqual(r.open.accessibilityCustomActions()?.first?.handler?(), true); XCTAssertEqual(s, 1) }
func testReuseReplacesOrdinaryHandler() { var a = 0, b = 0; let r = row(save: {a += 1}); configure(r, "B", save: {b += 1}); press(r.save); XCTAssertEqual(a, 0); XCTAssertEqual(b, 1) }

func testReenabledShortcut() { var s = 0; let r = row(save: {s += 1}); r.save.isEnabled = false; r.save.isEnabled = true; XCTAssertEqual(r.open.accessibilityCustomActions()?.first?.handler?(), true); XCTAssertEqual(s, 1) }

criteria.meets: Both ordinary and shortcut paths act once on the current owner/file and honor enabled state. Either refresh per-binding handlers with obsolete-binding rejection OR install a stable dispatcher that resolves current file/enabled state at activation. No particular token/helper/closure spelling required.
criteria.gap: An obsolete per-binding callback acts on a different/current rebound file, an obsolete captured owner acts unexpectedly, a disabled action still acts, or repeated setup causes duplicate dispatch. A correctly installed stable current-owner dispatcher is not an obsolete per-binding callback.
criteria.insufficient: If callback ownership/delay semantics are not specified, accept the explicitly documented safe current-owner design; do not invent a delayed per-binding rejection requirement. No absence-of-weak or speech/focus assertion is a hidden gate.
criteria.scope: A retained model action is invalidated by revision change. This is one per-binding strategy, not proof of enabled-state behavior or a requirement to reject a valid permanent current-owner dispatcher.

criteria.meets: Repeated setup replaces obsolete handlers and avoids duplicate calls or unintended ownership.

criteria.insufficient: A leak claim needs an appropriate lifetime assertion; absence of weak spelling alone is not a defect.
criteria.scope: Native BridgeOwner replaces callbacks and prevents old native-view dispatch. That does not by itself establish repeated SwiftUI action installation or lifetime of the complete row.
